name: regime_detection_vol_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms switch between passive accumulation (quiet low-vol regime) and aggressive directional execution (high-vol regime) in bursts visible at 5-second resolution. When 3-minute realized vol spikes above 2x the 10-minute baseline vol, it signals that aggressive directional flow has activated — the side confirmed by EMA_24 vs EMA_72 alignment predicts 15-25 spot point continuation over the next 30-120 seconds as the institutional order works through remaining fills. Conversely, when the vol ratio collapses back below the threshold (flow exhausted), price has overshot VWAP by 15-30 spot points and market makers who delta-hedged during the high-vol burst close their hedges, snapping price back toward VWAP within 60-90 seconds.

indicators.name: rv_short
indicators.purpose: 36 bars = 3 minutes of realized vol. This is the 'burst' window: when institutional flow switches from passive to aggressive, it saturates a 3-minute window before becoming visible on longer windows. The original HMM used 120 1-min bars (2 hours) to fit state transitions; at 5s we compress to the fast trigger — the 3-min window captures the activation, not the steady state.

indicators.name: rv_medium
indicators.purpose: 120 bars = 10 minutes of baseline realized vol. This establishes the session regime norm. Chosen to match the original's 120-bar HMM estimation window in time (120 × 1min vs 120 × 5s = only 10 min here). At 5s frequency, 10 minutes is sufficient to distinguish normal drift from burst — longer windows incorporate staleness from prior session dynamics.

indicators.name: vol_ratio
indicators.purpose: The ratio proxies the HMM's regime probability. When ratio > 2.0, the index has entered the high-vol regime (analogous to HMM P(high_vol) > 0.80). Ratio-based detection is stateless and avoids the computational complexity of forward-algorithm HMM estimation at 5-second frequency.

indicators.name: ema_fast
indicators.purpose: 24 bars = 2-minute EMA. Direction filter for momentum leg (low→high transition). 2-min window aligns with the regime activation window — if EMA_24 > EMA_72, the burst is in the bullish direction.

indicators.name: ema_slow
indicators.purpose: 72 bars = 6-minute EMA. Context filter providing the medium-term trend direction. Not extended to 15+ min because at 5s we are trading 30-120s continuation, not hour-long trends.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumulative(close * volume) / cumulative(volume), reset at session open
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP is a cumulative measure — no scaling needed. Used as mean-reversion anchor for the high→low transition leg. When vol collapses and price is displaced from VWAP, the snap-back is toward VWAP, not some arbitrary prior close.

conditions: MOMENTUM: vol_ratio crosses above vol_ratio_threshold (low→high transition) AND ema_fast > ema_slow (bullish EMA alignment)
REVERSION: vol_ratio crosses below vol_ratio_threshold (high→low transition) AND close < vwap * (1 - reversion_gap_threshold) (price below VWAP, snap-back expected)
MOMENTUM: vol_ratio crosses above vol_ratio_threshold (low→high transition) AND ema_fast < ema_slow (bearish EMA alignment)
REVERSION: vol_ratio crosses below vol_ratio_threshold (high→low transition) AND close > vwap * (1 + reversion_gap_threshold) (price above VWAP, snap-back expected)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. For momentum leg: if a vol burst reversal retraces 8 spot pts within 30 seconds, the thesis is wrong (the burst was noise, not institutional flow). For reversion leg: if price keeps moving away from VWAP by 8 more spot pts, the high-vol regime has not ended. Calibrated to typical NIFTY 30s move of 2-5 option pts — 4 pt stop allows normal noise while cutting true failures.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. For momentum: NIFTY vol-burst continuations average 15-25 spot pts; 14 captures ~60% of the median move (1:1.75 R:R). For reversion: VWAP snap-backs in moderate vol are 10-25 spot pts; 14 captures the lower half conservatively. Both legs share the same target since the expected move magnitudes overlap at 30-120s hold time.

filters.vix_filter: none — strategy uses intrinsic vol ratio for regime, not VIX
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; excludes first 15 minutes (pre-open noise, insufficient rv_medium history) and last 10 minutes (expiry day risk)
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume at 5s is noisy; vol ratio is the primary filter
filters.trend_filter: EMA_fast vs EMA_slow provides direction; no separate trend filter needed
filters.spread_filter: limit orders at candle close — no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — vol ratio threshold may need periodic recalibration as NIFTY's intraday vol structure changes seasonally; HMM-proxy is simpler than true HMM so it loses the sequence-pattern edge but gains stability

adaptation_notes: The original strategy uses a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) fitted daily on 120-bar sequences of 1-minute returns from NIFTY 50 constituent stocks. Three changes were made: (1) Universe shifted from individual stocks to NIFTY index — the regime transitions relevant to our 5-second option trades are index-level, not stock-level. (2) HMM replaced with vol_ratio (rv_short/rv_medium) — the HMM's regime probability is approximated by the ratio of 3-minute to 10-minute realized vol, capturing the same burst-vs-baseline distinction without forward-algorithm computation at every 5-second bar. (3) Hold time compressed from 10-45 min to 30-120s — the 5-second bar captures regime transitions earlier than the 1-minute bar, so we exit faster and reduce exposure. Two distinct signal legs preserved: momentum on low→high (original: EMA_8 > EMA_21 confirmation) and mean-reversion on high→low (original: price vs VWAP, RSI confirmation). RSI confirmation dropped since at 5-second bars RSI(14) = only 70 seconds of data — insufficient.
weaknesses: Vol ratio proxy loses the sequence-pattern information that the HMM captured — it cannot distinguish a sustained 3-minute vol burst from three brief 1-minute spikes that happen to sum to the same variance
NIFTY vol bursts near scheduled events (RBI, FOMC, earnings) are news-driven and may not respect EMA directional alignment — these transitions are unforecastable

Regime transitions can cluster: multiple low→high and high→low transitions per hour. With max_trades_per_day=5, high-frequency regime-switching days will exhaust the daily limit early and miss later cleaner signals
EMA_24 vs EMA_72 alignment can lag for the first transition of the day before adequate history accumulates (first 6 minutes of session)
